Package io.mavlink4j.transport

Interface MavlinkLink

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
RecordingLink, SerialLink, TcpClientLink, UdpListenLink, UdpTargetLink
public interface MavlinkLink extends AutoCloseable
Bytes in, bytes out. A MavlinkLink knows nothing about MAVLink frames — that is io.mavlink4j.codec's job — only how to move raw bytes over one physical or logical connection (UDP socket, TCP connection, eventually serial).

The LSP hinge: preservesMessageBoundaries()

This interface's real contract is "a byte stream with buffered resync," which a datagram link satisfies trivially (one poll(java.time.Duration) happens to return exactly one datagram's worth of bytes) and a stream link satisfies correctly (one poll(java.time.Duration) may return less than one frame, more than one frame, or a frame split across several polls). preservesMessageBoundaries() must never be read as "one poll = one message" — that promise would make TcpClientLink an unimplementable subtype of this interface. The flag exists only so the codec layer's FrameReader can decide how many resync buffers to keep (one per learned peer for a boundary-preserving link, exactly one for a stream link), never so a caller can skip resync.

Threading

Implementations are driven by exactly one reader thread calling poll(java.time.Duration) in a loop — that thread owns the read side. send(byte[], int, int, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer) is required to be thread-safe on every implementation because several services commonly share one link concurrently (a telemetry reader, a command sender and a manual-control relay all writing to the same socket).

Implementer contract: poll(java.time.Duration) returns null (never throws) on timeout or after close(); close() is idempotent and unblocks a pending poll; id() never changes; poll never returns a chunk it may later overwrite (see ByteChunk).

  • Method Details

    • id

      LinkId id()
      This link's stable identity for its whole life.

    • preservesMessageBoundaries

      boolean preservesMessageBoundaries()
      true for a datagram-shaped link (UDP: one underlying receive == one poll's worth of bytes), false for a stream-shaped link (TCP, eventually serial). See the class javadoc — this is a hint for the codec layer's resync bookkeeping, not a promise about frame boundaries.

    • poll

      ByteChunk poll(Duration timeout) throws IOException
      Blocks up to timeout for the next slice of bytes.
      Returns:
      the next ByteChunk, or null on timeout or because the link is closed — a closed link never throws for that reason, named after BlockingQueue.poll(long, java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit) whose return value carries the same "null means nothing available" contract. Only a genuine I/O failure throws.
      Throws:
      IOException - on a real socket/stream failure, not on timeout or close

    • send

      void send(byte[] frame, int off, int len, LinkPeer target) throws IOException
      Sends len bytes starting at off in frame to target. Thread-safe — see the class javadoc.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if target has no addressable peer (e.g. LinkPeer.NONE, or an unresolved host/port)
      IOException - on a genuine send failure

    • defaultTarget

      LinkPeer defaultTarget()
      This link's natural target when the caller has no more specific address in hand: the configured fixed destination for a dial-out link, the one connected remote for a stream link, or the most recently learned sender for a listen link (LinkPeer.NONE before anything has been heard).

    • close

      void close()
      Closes this link. Idempotent. Unblocks any thread currently parked in poll(java.time.Duration) by closing the underlying socket/stream out from under it, per this module's close-to-unblock-the-reader idiom — that thread's poll(java.time.Duration) then returns null rather than throwing. Declared to never throw (narrower than AutoCloseable.close(), which every implementation here honours) so try-with-resources works without a checked exception forcing every caller to handle one.
      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
